subject.title: Channel-friendly reauth for expired model logins

question: Should OpenClaw auto-start or auto-reuse a private device-code reauth flow after hard OpenAI/Codex auth failures, or should recovery remain explicit through `/login codex`?
rationale: Current main intentionally gates pairing-code delivery behind explicit owner/admin private commands; automatic recovery would change auth UX and security boundaries across channels.

options.title: Keep Explicit Default
options.body: Retain `/login codex` as the default recovery path and require a written security/product design before any automatic failure-triggered flow is implemented.

options.title: Allow Private Auto-Start
options.body: Permit hard auth failures in owner/admin private contexts to start or reuse a device-code flow immediately and report completion, expiry, or retry states in-channel.

options.title: Close As Command-Solved
options.body: Treat the merged explicit command path as sufficient for this narrower issue and leave automatic or brokered reauth to a broader auth-recovery issue.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Default
recommendation.body: Retain `/login codex` as the default recovery path and require a written security/product design before any automatic failure-triggered flow is implemented.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current `/login codex` implementation and provided the strongest maintainer-side proof for the Telegram privacy boundary.
